TRACKED ONLY TO 0.7.0b2: `PARITY.md:20-26` (no 0.7.x column past b2). MISSING: SubAgent TypedDict has no `mode` key (`libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/subagents.py:43-108`; grep 'isolated'|'fork' across SDK -> 0 hits); pagination fields never populated (grep `total_lines=|next_offset=` in backends/*.py -> 0); grep is time-bounded not 1,000-count-capped (`backends/filesystem.py:847-855`); TodoListMiddleware always-on (`graph.py:803, 897, 989`); test_deepagents_compat.py:79 checks the 0.6.12 __all__, no 0.7.13 name smoke test.
checked.delta: Add `mode: NotRequired[Literal['isolated','fork']]` to SubAgent and honour it in _create_task_tool; populate ReadResult pagination in Filesystem/State/Store backends and emit the 'N lines remaining / next offset' notice from read_file; add a 1,000-match `grep_max_count` cap with `truncated=True` alongside the time bound; make TodoListMiddleware opt-in via FeatureConfig (or a lean profile) while keeping bog's default; align rubric grader hook names with 0.7.11 (unverified); add a PARITY.md 0.7.13 column and a test that imports every 0.7.13 public name.
checked.why_killer: Anyone writing against deepagents 0.7 docs today can `pip install bog-agents` and keep their code, tests and tool-output parsers working, on Windows and with local models, which dcode does not offer. ROADMAP #26 was written before 0.7.0 shipped (2026-07-24); the bar has since moved through 13 patch releases including a breaking mode rename and rubric hooks.

checked.title: Token-diet profile with per-middleware prompt-token budget and CI regression gate
checked.evidence: Profile primitives for a lean harness exist: `HarnessProfile.base_system_prompt / system_prompt_suffix / tool_description_overrides / excluded_tools / excluded_middleware` at `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/profiles/harness/harness_profiles.py:550-634`, consumed in `graph.py:740, 903` — but no built-in `lean` profile (`profiles/harness/` holds only 5 model profiles; grep 'lean' -> 0). `/tokens` reports only 'System prompt + tools (fixed)' vs 'Conversation' (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/app.py:3275-3305`); no per-middleware attribution anywhere (grep `per.?middleware.*token|tokens_by_middleware` -> 0). Snapshot gate is prompt-text only: `libs/bog-agents/tests/unit_tests/smoke_tests/test_system_prompt.py` + `libs/bog-agents/Makefile:23-25 update-snapshots`; `Makefile:44 benchmark` target exists but no token/reward regression assertion.
checked.delta: Ship a built-in `lean` HarnessProfile (empty base prompt, trimmed tool descriptions, TodoList/plan tools excluded); add a `/tokens middleware` view that tokenizes each middleware's injected system-prompt segment and each tool schema and attributes them by middleware name; extend the smoke-test snapshot into a numeric baseline (base input tokens/turn per profile) that fails CI on regression, plus an optional harbor-reward gate; publish the numbers in docs.
checked.competitor: LangChain deepagents (65% cut, published eval); NVIDIA NOOA (half tokens); Google ADK Workflows
checked.why_killer: Local-model users on 8k-32k contexts get the room back that 100 middleware quietly consume, cost-sensitive solos pay less per turn, and teams can prove no quality regression instead of trusting a vendor blog. Nobody else can attribute tokens per middleware because nobody else has a middleware stack this deep.

checked.title: Governed Code Mode: sandboxed JS/Python `eval` with programmatic tool calling and `task()` subagent dispatch, gated by Expert Mode and the cost ledger
checked.evidence: none found after grepping `codeact|code_mode|CodeMode|quickjs|CodeInterpreter|programmatic.?tool|execute_python|run_code|python_repl` across libs/bog-agents, libs/cli, libs/partners (only .venv hits). ROADMAP.md #36 (lines ~530-536) and the 'Wave 4 satellites' note (~line 600) explicitly defer it. Governance hooks to reuse exist: Expert Mode asserts a `tool_call` fact per call at `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/expert_rules.py:333-337`; `CostLedger`/`RunawayCaps` at `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/cost_ledger.py:26-48`.
checked.delta: Build an interpreter middleware (QuickJS or a subprocess Python runner inside LocalSandbox/Docker) exposing an allowlisted `tools.*` namespace whose every call re-enters the normal tool path (so ExpertRulesMiddleware, SafeTools, HITL and CostLedger fire), plus a `task()` global that dispatches subagents/teams with a response schema and counts each spawn against RunawayCaps; add fan-out/vote helpers and a FeatureConfig toggle; tests must prove a denied rule blocks a tool call issued from code.
checked.competitor: LangChain deepagents CodeInterpreterMiddleware; Mastra createCodeMode; Pydantic harness Code Mode; OpenAI programmatic tool calling; NVIDIA NOOA
checked.why_killer: Users get N-way fan-out and vote patterns in a single round-trip instead of N tool calls, and enterprises get what nobody else has: code-mode calls that are still policy-checked and budget-counted. ROADMAP #36 predates competitor shipping; since 2026-07-21 deepagents, Mastra and Pydantic all shipped it, so it is now table stakes and the governance angle is the open flank.

checked.title: Forked subagents and forked team workers (inherit parent history + continuation preamble)
checked.evidence: `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/subagents.py:180-202` — comment and task-tool prompt state only the task description is forwarded and 'Each agent invocation is stateless'; SubAgent TypedDict (`subagents.py:43-108`) has no `mode` key; grep `\bfork\b|inherit.*history|parent_messages|continuation_preamble` across subagents.py, teams.py, team_executor.py, butcher.py -> 0 non-worktree hits. `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/teams.py:236 run_team` workers receive task text only; `libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/butcher.py` workers execute self-contained slice files. `sidechain.py:15-16 build_continuation_prompt` is the only continuation primitive and is for background-task resumption, not delegation.
checked.delta: Add `mode: 'isolated' | 'fork'` to SubAgent and CompiledSubAgent handling in `_create_task_tool` so a fork child receives the parent's full messages + identical system prompt + a continuation preamble (respecting private_state_field_names); default the general-purpose subagent to fork behind a user/global config toggle that is ignored when set from a project `.env`; extend `run_team` and butcher worker construction with the same option; add tests for history inheritance and the privacy rule.
checked.why_killer: A worker that already knows the diagnosis writes the fix instead of re-reading the repo, cutting tokens and wall time on every delegation; teams' fan-out workers stop duplicating the coordinator's investigation.
checked.duplicate_of: deepagents 0.7.13 parity pack: name-matched middleware override, isolated/fork subagent modes, delete + allowlist filesystem, output-format and backend-shim breaks

checked.title: Persistent spend limits: cross-session USD/token budgets with warn thresholds and user/project/org/daemon-job scopes
checked.evidence: In-session only: `budget_usd` cap on CostTracker `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/cost_tracker.py:200-240` (FeatureConfig.budget_usd `feature_config.py:136`); RBAC per-role `max_budget_usd` `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/enterprise.py:63`; team-run `CostLedger(caps=RunawayCaps(max_cost_usd=...))` in memory `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/cost_ledger.py:26-48, 133-159` wired at `libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/team_executor.py:220` and `app.py:11044-11056`. No persistence (grep save/load/sqlite in cost_ledger.py -> 0), no daily/monthly windows, no warn-at-percent, no per-request max_cost callback, no daemon job budget (`libs/daemon/bog_agents_daemon/models.py` has max_retries only), no `/cost budget` (grep budget in commands/*.py -> only thinking_budget), no headless `/cost` (`headless_commands.py` grep cost -> 0).
checked.delta: Add a durable `SpendLedger` (SQLite beside sessions.db) keyed by scope (user/project/org/daemon-job) with daily/monthly USD+token ceilings and `warn_at_percent`, replay-safe (dedupe on checkpoint/run id); route CostTracker + CostLedger entries into it and consult it before each model call; add `AmbientJob.budget_usd` to the daemon; expose `/cost budget [set|show]` with a headless twin and per-model/provider breakdown; audit-log every block.
checked.competitor: Mastra TokenCostControl; Pydantic harness Spend Limits; Google ADK ADK_MAX_LLM_CALLS; OpenAI per-checkpoint usage isolation
checked.why_killer: A solo user sets '$5/day' once and never sees a surprise bill from an overnight daemon job; an enterprise gets org-scoped ceilings with an audit line for every block. Competitors moved from run caps to scoped monetary budgets in August; bog already owns the ledger, so this is a short hop to leapfrog.

Transport is `StreamableHttpConnection` via langchain-mcp-adapters (`mcp_tools.py:527-546`). Trust is config-fingerprint based only (`mcp_trust.py:31-147`); SafeTools/ExpertRules have no annotation inputs (grep annotation|destructive in safe_tools.py, expert_rules.py -> 0).
checked.delta: Bump to an `mcp` SDK release that implements the 2026-07-28 revision (unverified availability), then: honour `server/discover` + stateless sessions, subscribe to `subscriptions/listen`, cache tools/list per `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` with a deterministic sort for prompt caching, poll the Tasks extension for long-running calls, map `input_required` elicitations onto bog's HITL interrupt/dialog, feed `destructiveHint`/`readOnlyHint` into SafeToolsMiddleware auto-approval and as Expert Mode `tool_call` fact fields, and switch mcp_oauth.py from DCR to Client ID Metadata Documents.
checked.competitor: LangChain 1.4 MCPAdapter; Mastra 1.60; Microsoft Agent Framework dotnet-1.19 (Tasks)

checked.title: Durable runs on LangGraph 1.2 primitives: graceful drain on SIGTERM, per-node timeouts, saga error handlers, DeltaChannel history, fork/resume runs
checked.evidence: SHIPPED: langgraph 1.2.9 pinned (`libs/bog-agents/uv.lock:1673-1674`, `pyproject.toml:38`); DeltaChannel on messages `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/graph.py:21, 90` + `_messages_reducer.py:1-53`; daemon SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers + HTTP /shutdown `libs/daemon/bog_agents_daemon/main.py:152-223`; `/rewind to <checkpoint>` seeds a NEW thread from any checkpoint and resumes it `libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/app.py:7043, 7160-7212` (driven from tests/unit_tests/test_app.py). PARTIAL/MISSING: daemon drain only waits 30s then cancels in-flight tasks — no checkpoint-and-resume (`main.py:236-244`; `runner.py` grep checkpoint|resume -> 0); `session_fork.py` (create_fork/list_forks) has zero callers in the package (grep -> tests only); `RunControl.request_drain`, `TimeoutPolicy`, `error_handler -> Command` compensation: grep across SDK/CLI/daemon -> 0.
checked.delta: Wire LangGraph 1.2 `RunControl.request_drain()` into the daemon shutdown and TUI Ctrl+C paths so an in-flight run checkpoints at the next node boundary and is marked RESUMABLE (then resume on restart instead of stamping FAILED); apply `TimeoutPolicy` to model/tool nodes with shell timeouts delegated to background_shell; add an `error_handler` that reverts checkpoint commits on failure; expose `/session fork` (reusing the existing /rewind seeding path or session_fork.py) and a daemon `runs/{id}/resume` endpoint.
checked.competitor: LangGraph 1.2; Pydantic AI @durable_operation + step persistence; OpenAI RunState; Mastra durable agent execution
checked.why_killer: A daemon restart or Ctrl+C mid-job resumes where it stopped instead of failing the run, and week-long threads stop growing the checkpoint DB quadratically. ROADMAP #39 predates these primitives landing in LangGraph itself; adopting them removes a chunk of bespoke code.

checked.title: Tool-result prompt-injection defender and quarantine policy
checked.evidence: none found after grepping `prompt.?injection|quarantine|indirect.?injection|untrusted.?content|ToolResultGuard` (only comments, e.g. `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/memory.py:224`). Nearest pieces are different features: DLPMiddleware scans model-call messages for PII/secrets (`libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/dlp.py:1-25, 214`); GuardrailMiddleware runs only in `wrap_model_call` over the last human text and the response (`libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/guardrails/middleware.py:48-60, 99`); Expert Mode asserts only `tool_call` facts (`middleware/expert_rules.py:333`, `expert_engine/working_memory.py:38`); web/MCP tool outputs are not wrapped as untrusted (grep untrusted in mcp_tools.py -> only server-trust messages at :873, 908).
checked.delta: Add a `ToolResultDefenderMiddleware` in `wrap_tool_call` that scores each ToolMessage from web/MCP/untrusted-path reads with a heuristic + optional local-model classifier, asserts a `tool_result` fact (source, score, verdict) so YAML expert rules can quarantine/redact/require-approval, rewrites quarantined content in the persisted ToolMessage, and appends a quarantine entry to EvidenceBundle/causal ledger; wire into create_cli_agent behind a FeatureConfig flag with tests for a poisoned README and a poisoned MCP response.
checked.competitor: Pydantic AI harness PromptInjectionDefender; Mastra processToolResult guardrails; Google ADK Model Armor plugin; OpenAI v0.22.0 redaction
checked.why_killer: A poisoned README or MCP response cannot silently steer the run, and a regulated team gets a per-run evidence line for every quarantined result. Three competitors shipped this in a four-week span after OpenAI's sandbox-escape disclosure; bog can do it without cloud calls (local model) and with declarative policy.

checked.title: Explainable Auto approval mode: deterministic allow + batched model review + human fallback, with every decision as an Expert Mode fact
checked.evidence: SHIPPED: shift+tab permission cycle default/accept-edits/plan (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/app.py:797-838`); deterministic AutoModeRuleEngine + consolidated git classifier (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/auto_mode.py:349-407`, tests/unit_tests/test_auto_mode_rules.py); Haiku risk eval with not-found fallback (`auto_mode.py:208-223, 459-554`); ASK verdict falls through to the human dialog (`auto_mode.py:486`, `textual_adapter.py:760-800`). GAPS: classifier is hard-coded to `claude-haiku-4-5*` — no per-provider default, no local model (`auto_mode.py:212-213`); the 'batch' loop evaluates each request separately, not one structured batched decision (`textual_adapter.py:783-800`); no repeated-denial/timeout escalation; decisions are not recorded as Expert Mode facts or audit entries (grep AutoDecision+audit/assert_fact -> 0; `expert_controller.py:158 assert_fact` exists but is unused for approvals).
checked.delta: Replace per-call haiku_risk_eval with a single structured batched review (all pending tool calls + user's stated outcome) via a per-provider default classifier resolved from the active model provider (Anthropic/OpenAI/Ollama/Bedrock), keep narrow deterministic allows as a bypass, add a denial/timeout counter that drops back to the human prompt, and assert an `approval_decision` fact (rule_source, classifier verdict, reason) into the Expert Mode engine + causal ledger so `/why` and `/prove` can explain and audit it.
checked.competitor: LangChain deepagents-code Auto mode; Microsoft Agent Framework Harness (standing rules + heuristic auto-approval)
checked.why_killer: Fewer interruptions without going YOLO, and, unlike dcode, every 'why did it let that through' has an answer. Bog already has permission-mode cycling, SafeTools, exec_risk and the rule engine; the missing piece is the batched model reviewer and the audit trail.

checked.title: Plugin marketplaces with Claude/Codex manifests, per-plugin auto-update, and a Python ExtensionAPI that can register middleware
checked.evidence: SHIPPED: extension manifest bundling skills+hooks+mcp_servers+commands+agents (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/extensions.py:25-72`), install from local dir or git URL (`extensions.py:193-235`, `extensibility.py:122-136`; tests/unit_tests/test_extensions.py); `plugin_marketplace.py:151-168` local-path copy only; Claude Code skill/MCP import (`claude_code_compat.py:177-337`). MISSING: HTTPS JSON catalogues, owner/repo@tag resolution, per-plugin autoUpdate (grep auto_?update -> 0), Python ExtensionAPI / register_middleware / register_backend_route / on_shutdown (grep -> 0; the only entry-point loader is for profiles at `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/profiles/_builtin_profiles.py:238`), trust-store gating of installs (grep trust in extensions.py/extensibility.py -> 0), headless `bog-agents plugin` twin (`headless_commands.py` grep plugin -> 0).
checked.delta: Add marketplace sources (GitHub owner/repo@tag via `gh`/git, HTTPS JSON catalogue with signature) and `autoUpdate` per plugin persisted in the extensions registry; define a Python `ExtensionAPI` (register_middleware/register_tool/register_backend_route/on_shutdown) loaded from a manifest `python:` entry and injected into create_cli_agent's extra middleware, gated by the existing skill-trust store (ask/always/never) and the self-modification guard; add a headless `bog-agents plugin` command.
checked.why_killer: A team publishes one marketplace repo and every member installs recipes, MCP servers, hooks and a custom middleware with one command, gated by trust policy. ROADMAP #34/#35 proposed an importer and registry; dcode has since shipped marketplaces plus a middleware-capable extension API, which maps directly onto bog's middleware-first architecture.

checked.title: Windows-native sandbox launcher (no WSL/Docker) and a published Windows support matrix
checked.evidence: CI already runs a Linux+Windows matrix (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:49-57`, self-hosted runners). `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/sandbox/local_sandbox.py:94-97`: 'Windows has no launcher yet (AppContainer wiring is tracked as ROADMAP #22)' — `require_sandbox` fails closed there. `libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/doctor.py:441-456` checks only bwrap/seatbelt; no `--windows` mode (grep windows|sandbox in doctor_deep.py -> 0). none found after grepping `AppContainer|JobObject|CreateRestrictedToken|restricted token` in SDK/CLI. README has a CI badge but no support matrix (`README.md:10`).
checked.delta: Implement a Windows launcher in local_sandbox.py (Job Object + restricted token or AppContainer, filesystem ACLs on working_dir, read-deny paths, secret-env stripping reused) selected by `SandboxConfig.build_local_sandbox` on win32, keep egress through the existing CONNECT allowlist proxy; add `bog-agents doctor --windows` checks; publish a Windows support matrix and per-OS CI badge; add Windows-only tests for confinement.
checked.competitor: LangChain deepagents-code (unsupported on Windows); OpenAI Agents SDK UnixLocal (macOS/Linux only); Microsoft Agent Framework shell tooling (alpha)
checked.why_killer: Bog becomes the only harness a Windows developer can run sandboxed on the machine in front of them; every competitor either says 'use WSL', requires Docker, or ships shell tooling as alpha. This is an open flank that also unblocks regulated desktops that forbid WSL/Docker.

checked.title: Warn-on-cache-bust for every model call plus provider cache affinity (Bedrock, Fireworks, local KV cache)
checked.evidence: SHIPPED: `/compact`/`/clear` cache-break warnings only (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/prompt_cache.py:31-61`; tests/unit_tests/test_prompt_cache.py); AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware always appended (`libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/graph.py:244-250`); Bedrock prompt caching when langchain-aws present (`graph.py:219-266`); cache read/write tokens tracked and printed (`middleware/cost_tracker.py:183-196, 321-326, 529-542`). MISSING: per-call stable-prefix hash / bust detector and offending-middleware attribution (grep `cache.?bust|prefix.?hash|stable.?prefix` -> 0); prefix hit-rate in `/cost` (grep hit.?rate -> 0); Fireworks session affinity (only a model-id string at `profiles/harness/_nvidia_nemotron_3_ultra.py:50`); no explicit byte-stability guarantee for llama.cpp/vLLM.
checked.delta: Add an innermost `CacheBustDetectorMiddleware` that hashes the system prompt + message prefix up to the cache boundary each call, diffs against the previous turn, and warns naming the middleware whose injected segment changed; compute prefix hit-rate from cache_read/input tokens and show it in `/cost` and the status bar; add Fireworks session-affinity header support and a test asserting the sweeper/summarizer keep the prefix byte-stable for local providers.
checked.competitor: Pydantic AI harness Warn On Cache Busts; LangChain deepagents 0.7 Bedrock/Fireworks caching; MCP deterministic tool ordering
checked.why_killer: Cost drops without changing prompts, and local-model users get KV-cache reuse that turns a 30-second turn into a 5-second one. Bog's street-sweeper invariant (never change message count/order) was designed for exactly this; surfacing the hit rate makes the benefit visible.

checked.title: Sandbox templates with warm repo checkouts, snapshots, run-scoped workdirs and network-off, for daemon and CI-red repair jobs
checked.evidence: A local Docker provider exists (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/integrations/docker.py:106-351`, factory `integrations/sandbox_factory.py:70-204`; tests/unit_tests/test_docker_sandbox_arg.py) but `docker run` passes only --name/--memory/--cpus/-v/-w/--rm (`docker.py:215-252`) — no `--network none`, no image commit/snapshot, no template cache. `sandbox_config.py:20-71` declares `snapshot`, `preinstall`, `network_allowlist`; the factory consumes preinstall + allowlist (`sandbox_factory.py:82-124`) but `.snapshot` has zero consumers (grep `\.snapshot\b` -> only unrelated background_shell/drive hits). Daemon runs a non-sandbox FilesystemBackend with no shell for unattended triggers (`libs/daemon/bog_agents_daemon/runner.py:405-453`) and AmbientJob has no sandbox/provider field (`models.py` grep sandbox -> 0).
checked.delta: Add named templates to DockerProvider (build-once image with repo checkout + deps, keyed by sandbox.toml `snapshot`), `docker commit`-based snapshot/restore, run-scoped `/workspace/<run-id>` workdirs, `--network none` or allowlist-only via the egress proxy, and persist sandbox id in the run record so a resumed daemon job reattaches; add an `AmbientJob.sandbox` field and use it for daemon triggers and the #30 CI-red repair path.
checked.competitor: Mastra 1.60/1.64 sandbox checkpoints + templates; OpenAI Agents SDK snapshots + Docker network-off; deepagents-code remote sandboxes
checked.why_killer: Scheduled jobs start in seconds on a warm checkout instead of cloning and installing every time, and untrusted-repo runs are isolated by default, which the August OpenAI escape made a purchasing question.

checked.title: Advisor tool and self-extension: escalate one question to a stronger model mid-run, and let the agent author and persist a new skill/capability
checked.evidence: No advisor tool: grep `ask_advisor|advisor` -> only `audit_advisor_id` (financial-advisor audit field, `libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/builder.py:97`); operator mode swaps the model for the whole turn, not one question (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/operator_mode.py:57-119`). Self-extension pieces exist but are user-driven: `/expert write` LLM-authored expert rules with lint, dry-run and human approve before disk write (`libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/expert_engine/authoring.py:1-30, 402`; tests/unit_tests/test_expert_authoring.py); `/teach` records a session and generates a skill file (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/teach.py:109`); self-modification guard #24 SHIPPED (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/self_protection.py:1-79`, wired `agent.py:2096`, tests/unit_tests/test_self_protection.py; batch-tool bypass SAFE-1 closed via `middleware/permissions.py:183 _multi_edit_targets`).
checked.delta: Add an `ask_advisor` tool that sends a bounded question (+ optional context excerpt) to the operator preset's `hard` tier model and returns the answer as a ToolMessage, counted in CostLedger/CostTracker and capped by RunawayCaps; add an agent-callable `propose_skill`/`propose_rule` path that drafts into `.bog-agents/` staging, runs the existing authoring lint/dry-run, and requires HITL + trust-store approval before activation (self_protection.py already blocks silent writes).
checked.competitor: Pydantic AI harness Advisor + Capability Creation
checked.why_killer: A local or cheap model runs the loop and the user pays a frontier model only for the one hard question, and repeated workflows turn into reusable skills without hand-authoring, while the self-modification guard keeps it from rewriting its own rules.

checked.title: Tamper-evident action log and OTel GenAI export as a compliance artefact
checked.evidence: SHIPPED pieces: append-only per-session JSONL causal ledger recording tool calls, rule fires and final answers (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/causal/ledger.py:8-12, 127, 225`; `causal/middleware.py:128-145`; tests/unit_tests/test_causal.py); `AuditTrailMiddleware.export_json` with sha256 content fingerprints (`libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/audit_trail.py:248-254, 301`); HMAC-SHA-256-sealed compliance reports (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/compliance/__init__.py:15-26`, test_compliance.py); Ed25519-signed TraceFile export/verify (`libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/tracefile/signing.py`, `controller.py:10, 258`, test_tracefile.py). MISSING: per-entry hash chain (grep `prev_hash|hash_chain` -> 0), retention policy (grep retention -> only 'unbounded retention' note at audit_trail.py:104-113), approval decisions and cost entries in one log (causal ledger has no approval/cost events — grep -> 0), OTel: only LangSmith OTEL span exporter (`libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/langsmith_integration.py:106-107`), `_observability.py:26` states 'no OpenTelemetry'; no gen_ai semconv or traceparent (grep -> 0); no opentelemetry dependency in either pyproject.
checked.delta: Extend the causal ledger into a hash-chained per-run JSONL (each event carries sha256(prev)), add approval-decision, Expert Mode verdict and cost events, a retention/rotation policy (6-month default) and a signed export command reusing tracefile's Ed25519 signer; add a vendor-neutral OTLP exporter emitting GenAI semconv spans (model/tool/middleware/subagent with cost attributes) with LangSmith as one exporter, and propagate `traceparent` through MCP `_meta`.
checked.competitor: Microsoft Agent Framework (OTel semconv consolidation), Google ADK experimental token telemetry, Pydantic AI OTel GenAI spans
checked.why_killer: A regulated buyer can export a signed, reconstructable record of what the agent did and who approved it, which no competitor packages as a single artefact; the Digital Omnibus deferral (Annex III to 2027-12-02) buys time but procurement questionnaires already ask.
